ash: Heads-up — after landing kernel_autoselect_v3 we saw a ~12-18% p95 latency regression on long-seq streaming (seq=2048) workloads that are kv-cache heavy. Perfetto trace: https://perfetto.link/abcd1234 :thinking_face:

kyle: Looking at the nsys capture I pulled (attached), the timeline shows a new 'fused_flash_v3' GEMM kicking in but the write phase of kV cache kernels is now serialized more often. nsys summary (short):
```
# nsys timeline extract
fused_flash_v3        38.2ms  (kernel)
kv_write_stage        21.6ms  (kernel, repeated x3)
flash_attn_bwd        12.7ms
cutlass_gemm_large    44.9ms
SM util ~78%, but stalls on L2->DRAM
```

jenna: Can you paste the exact nsys command you used? I want the cpu/gpu timeline, and cudaMemCpy details. Also which machine type? nvlink vs PCIe matters for KV write stalls.

ash: Ran on g5.12x large (no nvlink). Command: `nsys profile --sample=cpu --output=nsys_reg_kv_v3 ./run_infer --profile-seq 2048 --num-requests 64` — exported trace to perfetto link above.

misha: Two quick hypotheses: (1) kernel_autoselect picked fused_flash_v3 for fp16 path but its shared-mem tiling increases register pressure causing slower tail KV writes; (2) batching heuristic widened window to 7ms which mixes small and big batches causing more KV write contention.

devon: Ran an A/B locally: revert just the kernel selector -> p95 drops back by 14% (195ms -> 168ms). Reverting batching window -> p95 improves ~6%. Small experiment logs:
```
baseline (master pre-change): p95=168ms throughput=120 req/s
with kernel_autoselect_v3: p95=196ms throughput=125 req/s
with only batching_v2 (wider window): p95=180ms throughput=132 req/s
revert kernel selector only: p95=171ms throughput=118 req/s
```

kyle: Interesting that throughput rises while p95 worsens — indicates more batching but worse tail. Could be more aggressive batch coalescing that increases per-request stall when kv_write serializes.

jenna: Suggest next steps: capture `nvprof --kernels` or `nsight` with metrics (gld_efficiency, gst_efficiency, l2_read_hit_rate). Also dump kernel launch params for fused_flash_v3 and compare shared mem / regs per thread. Can someone run: `cuobjdump --dump-sass fused_flash_v3.o` and `cupti metrics`?

ash: I'll run a narrow repro with nvprof and perf counters. Also dropping batching window to 3ms brings p95 back close to baseline in a quick test. I'll post traces.

perf-bot: Incident note created: PERF-2026-214 — investigating attention kernel regression (linked traces and nsys captures). :spiral_calendar:

misha: If fused_flash_v3 is the culprit we can try two short-term mitigations: build a variant with smaller tile that reduces register pressure (likely slower peak but better KV overlap) or fallback to fused_flash_v2 for seq>1024. We should also add an objective check in rollout: ensure p95 on kv-heavy evalset doesn't regress >5%.

devon: Agreed. I'll prototype a small-tile compile and run CI microbench. If that helps tail we can ship as opt-in flag for kernel_autoselect.

ash: Thanks team — will upload nvprof/ncu output and a trimmed perfetto trace with highlights in next 2 hours. Ping me for repro scripts if you want to iterate locally. :thumbsup:
